blogs.title: FlashAttention-3, Explained: Why Your Transformer’s Bottleneck Just Got 2x Faster
blogs.description: A plain-language tour of what attention is, why it’s the slowest part of Transformers, and how FlashAttention-3 accelerates it on modern GPUs. Covers the headline results (up to 2.0x over FA-2, 75% H100 utilization, ~1.2 PFLOPs/s in FP8) and what that means for long-context models, training, and inference.

blogs.title: Asynchrony on Hopper: Warp Specialization and Ping-Pong Scheduling Made Simple
blogs.description: Breaks down how Hopper’s Tensor Cores and Tensor Memory Accelerator run asynchronously—and how FlashAttention-3 splits producer/consumer warps to hide memory and instruction latency. Explains the ‘ping-pong’ scheduling trick that overlaps GEMMs and softmax for higher utilization, with intuitive diagrams and analogies.

blogs.title: Overlapping GEMM and Softmax: The Two-Stage Pipeline That Squeezes More From Tensor Cores
blogs.description: Dives into the intra-warpgroup 2-stage pipeline that interleaves blockwise matmuls with softmax operations. Explains the dependency-breaking buffer strategy, how waits/commits are orchestrated, the trade-offs with register pressure, and why a 3-stage variant is tempting but tricky.

blogs.title: FP8 Without the Faceplants: Block Quantization and Incoherent Processing for Accurate Attention
blogs.description: Explains why naive FP8 attention can be numerically fragile, especially with LLM outliers, and how FlashAttention-3 fixes it. Walks through block quantization and the randomized orthogonal transform (Hadamard + sign flips) to spread outliers, achieving up to 2.6x lower error than standard FP8 baselines.

blogs.title: From Layouts to Throughput: The Kernel Engineering Behind FP8 FlashAttention-3
blogs.description: A practitioner’s look at making FP8 fast: k-major constraints, in-kernel V transposes via LDSM/STSM, accumulator-to-operand register permutations, and avoiding costly pre/post kernels. Shows how these micro-choices unlock near-2x GEMM throughput and keep the pipeline fed.

blogs.title: Benchmarks That Matter: FA-3 vs FA-2 vs cuDNN on H100
blogs.description: Summarizes the paper’s performance results across sequence lengths, head dims, and masking. Interprets TFLOPs/s, utilization, and where FA-3 wins or ties vendor kernels. Offers guidance on when to pick FP16 vs FP8 and what to expect in real workloads.

blogs.title: What Faster Attention Unlocks: Long Contexts, New Modalities, and Cheaper Training
blogs.description: Connects the speedups to user-visible gains—longer contexts for code and documents, more efficient video/audio transformers, and better training economics. Discusses how higher utilization changes batch/sequence trade-offs and where bottlenecks move next.

blogs.title: Adopting FlashAttention-3: Practical Tips for PyTorch and HF Users
blogs.description: A hands-on integration guide: where FA-3 fits in the stack, expected drop-in benefits, and knobs that matter (tile sizes, precision modes, masking). Notes on compatibility, numerical behavior (FP32 softmax accumulators), and how to profile to confirm wins.

blogs.title: Inside the Backward Pass: Keeping Gradients Fast With Asynchrony
blogs.description: Explains how the ideas that speed up the forward pass (tiling, asynchrony, overlapping) carry into the backward pass, which has more GEMMs. Highlights the 1.5–1.75x gains over FA-2 and practical implications for end-to-end training time.

blogs.title: Beyond Hopper: Why FlashAttention-3’s Ideas Generalize to Future Accelerators
blogs.description: Discusses the portability of the approach—what relies on Hopper-specific features and what generalizes to any architecture with async execution and low-precision tensor cores. Sets expectations for Blackwell/FP4-era attention and directions for community kernels.
